title: Dal Tadka
subtitle: Indian spiced lentil dal with a tempered butter and cumin finish
excerpt: The everyday comfort food of the Indian subcontinent: red lentils simmered to a smooth, soupy consistency with turmeric and ginger, then lifted at the end by a sputtering tadka of butter or ghee, cumin seeds, garlic, and dried chilli poured sizzling over the top.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal tadka (tadka means tempering — the technique of frying spices in hot fat to release their fragrance before adding to a dish) is one of the most universally eaten dishes across the Indian subcontinent. Red lentils (masoor dal) dissolve quickly during cooking to produce a smooth, thick soup; yellow split peas (chana dal) or toor dal remain more distinct. The tadka is the key transformation: the sizzling of whole cumin seeds and garlic in hot ghee or butter, which is then poured over the cooked lentils, produces an immediate fragrance and flavour change. Dal tadka is eaten daily in millions of homes across India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the diaspora worldwide.

recipeTools.notes: A medium saucepan, plus a small pan for the tadka.

content.text: Do not add salt until the lentils are fully cooked: salt during cooking can prevent lentils softening. The tadka must be made just before serving and poured over immediately while still sizzling; the sputtering hot fat hitting the surface of the dal is part of the effect. Use ghee for the most flavourful result; unsalted butter is an acceptable substitute.

items.preparation: rinsed until the water runs clear
2 finely chopped for the base; 2 thinly sliced for the tadka

content.text: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden. Add the 2 chopped garlic cloves and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, cumin, and chilli powder and cook for 30 seconds. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.

Add the rinsed lentils and 1 litre of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and beginning to dissolve. Add salt and garam masala. Stir well and taste. If the dal is too thick, add a little more water; it should be pourable but not watery.

Make the tadka: melt the butter in a small pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until sputtering. Add the sliced garlic and whole dried chillies and cook for 30 seconds until the garlic is golden. Pour the entire sizzling tadka over the dal immediately. Squeeze over the lemon juice, scatter with coriander, and serve with rice or roti.
